decisions.match: superior division of the left middle cerebral artery
decisions.answer: Inferior Frontal gyrus of Dominant Hemisphere
decisions.reason: Non-fluent, effortful speech with PRESERVED comprehension after a superior-division MCA stroke is Broca (expressive) aphasia, which localises to the inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere. June 2025 keyed inferior temporal lobe — that is Wernicke's area, and would give fluent speech with impaired comprehension. December 2024 is correct.

decisions.match: chronic renal failure presents with pallor fatigue lethargy and pedal edema
decisions.reason: Normocytic anaemia (MCV 86 fL) with raised ferritin in chronic renal failure is anaemia of chronic disease: treat the EPO deficit and replete iron. June 2025 keyed B12 replacement, which would give macrocytosis. December 2024 is correct.

decisions.match: expressionless face a resting pill rolling tremor
decisions.reason: Pill-rolling rest tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia and a shuffling gait is idiopathic Parkinson disease. June 2025 keyed Huntington disease, which produces chorea and is typically younger-onset. December 2024 is correct.

decisions.match: spontaneous bloody discharge from her right nipple
decisions.reason: Spontaneous unilateral bloody nipple discharge with a retroareolar nodule in a 36-year-old is an intraductal papilloma, the commonest benign cause. June 2025 keyed intraductal carcinoma. December 2024 is correct.

answers: branched chain alpha keto acid dehydrogenase
decisions.reason: MSUD is deficiency of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex, so valine, leucine and isoleucine are implicated. Phenylalanine points to PKU and methionine to homocystinuria, so 'all of the above' cannot be right. December 2025 is wrong.

decisions.match: The medial cord of the brachial plexus continues as which of the following nerves
decisions.reason: The medial cord's terminal continuation is the ulnar nerve; the medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm and medial pectoral nerve branch from it earlier. As a single-best-answer item the ulnar nerve is correct. FCPS-I repeats this three times with two different keys, so majority voting is unsafe here and the item was adjudicated directly.

decisions.match: In the early pathological stages of acute appendicitis
decisions.reason: Acute appendicitis characteristically produces suppurative inflammation; gangrenous change is a later complication of vascular compromise, not the early picture.

decisions.match: severe pain in the ankle and develops ecchymosis on the second day
decisions.reason: The patient can still stand on the toes, so the Achilles tendon is intact. Sudden ankle pain with delayed bruising and a normal heel-rise is a plantaris rupture (tennis leg).
